_comment: The server-driven sidebar menu. GET /spark/program-units filters this per caller before it
reaches the client, so a unit whose target the caller has no right to never appears -- hosts
write zero router links for navigation.
Home is a persistentObject unit with an objectId, which makes it a deep link to one page
(/po/home/main) rather than a list. The id is any stable string the app chooses; HomeActions
receives it as OnLoadAsync's id argument and ignores it -- there is exactly one Home.
There is deliberately NO url unit for the 'install the GitHub App' link. Its address is
per-environment (coveragedevelopment vs coverageproduction, resolved from configuration at
request time), and this file is static -- a hardcoded slug would point a developer's machine
at the production App. That link stays in the Angular extra content on the Home page, where
it comes from /api/me/accounts and is correct in every environment.
There is deliberately NO 'Project boards' unit either. Boards are reached through the account
that owns them -- Account's 'account-projects' sub-query -- which is where a user already is
when they care about one, and which scopes the list to that account for free. A top-level unit
listed every board the caller could see, one click from Home, duplicating the sub-query with a
less useful shape. The GetGitHubProjects query stays declared and granted, so /query/github-
projects still answers a direct link; it simply has no menu entry.
The Administration group (#504, M5b) holds the host metrics dashboard and the commit-graph mirrors. Both targets
are granted to Administrators alone (Read/HostMetrics through dashboards:administrators, QueryRead/
RepositoryGraphState directly), so for everyone else the group is empty and not shown. The dashboards package adds
its own Dashboards > Database entry under the same rule.
The Guides group holds the static how-to pages, each an Angular route of its own and open to anonymous visitors:
the merge queue's GitHub setup (/merge-queue/setup), the dependency updater's setup (/dependency-updates/setup)
and connecting an AI agent to /mcp (/connect-agent, also the topbar's button). A url unit has no target to grant,
so the group is shown to everyone. The merge queue unit kept its id when it moved here from the Coverage group.
